title: Data structures
description: Purpose, guarantees, costs and use-case recognition for each structure, independent of a particular pattern.

nodes.name: Array
nodes.description: Contiguous storage: O(1) random access, O(n) insert/delete by shifting; doubles as a direct-address table for bounded values.

facets.recognize: Uses an array as a frequency/visited table when values are bounded (e.g. 1..n) instead of a hashmap.
facets.explain: States access/insert/delete costs and why middle insertion is O(n).
facets.implement: Reads, writes and shifts elements correctly.

misconceptions.desc: Assumed inserting or deleting in the middle is O(1).
Used a hashmap when values are bounded and a plain array would be simpler and faster.

nodes.name: Sorted array properties
nodes.description: Monotonic order: duplicates are adjacent, pairs can be found with converging pointers, two sorted arrays merge linearly.

facets.recognize: Notices sorted input and exploits it (two pointers, merge, adjacent duplicates, binary search).
facets.explain: States which properties sortedness guarantees and what sorting destroys (original indices).

misconceptions.desc: Ignored that input is sorted; used hashing or nested loops instead of a linear pass.
Sorted the input when original indices are part of the answer (e.g. Two Sum returning indices).

nodes.name: Matrix (2D grid)
nodes.description: Rows, columns, diagonals, layers/boundaries; square vs rectangular; properties like transpose symmetry.

facets.recognize: Identifies the structure an algorithm needs: layers, boundaries, transpose, first row/column as storage.
facets.explain: Knows how a transpose or row reversal moves each (i, j).
facets.implement: Traverses by row, column, diagonal and boundary.

misconceptions.desc: Assumed a square matrix where m != n is allowed.

nodes.name: Hash map
nodes.description: Key -> value lookup in O(1) average; used for frequency counts and value -> index lookup.

facets.recognize: Reaches for a hashmap for counting, value -> index lookup or 'seen before?' with unbounded values; also knows when O(1) space beats it.
facets.explain: States the trade: O(n) extra space for O(1) average lookup.
facets.implement: Designs the key/value pair that answers the question (value -> index vs value -> count).

misconceptions.desc: Stored the wrong mapping (index -> value instead of value -> index).
Used a hashmap where O(1) extra space is achievable (Boyer-Moore, XOR, math, two pointers).

nodes.name: Hash set
nodes.description: Membership and de-duplication in O(1) average.

facets.recognize: Uses a set for membership or dedupe, and knows when duplicates must be counted instead.

misconceptions.desc: Used a set where the count of duplicates matters.
